items.title: Hypolite Charles Interview, 1963-04-13
items.q: And we had some trumpet player there, but Matoyi was always the one that was picked for the cadence.

ctx.x: rehearsals, you see. And then we'd play those concerts. Did you try your jazz compositions too as a whole group? No, no. It was just a song. Just a song. That's right.

Because Mr. Moret couldn't play no jazz, you see. He never did play no jazz. And whenever he'd have those concerts like that, there wasn't no jazz at all. And this fellow I'm telling you about, Matoyi, he's the one who used to do all the cadence work. He did? Yes. And we had some trumpet player there, but Matoyi was always the one that was picked for the cadence. Oh. But he went down, huh? Oh yeah. But I don't want him to go down if they don't hold up.
Yeah. How often did you have vocalists performing with your group outside of your instrumentals?
